harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent name-based Apache sites on node1: docs.branch.test and orders.branch.test share TCP 8080, unknown hosts return HTTP 403, and cross-tenant files return 404. SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld permits 8080, SSH remains healthy, staged content is unchanged, and all behavior survived a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed Apache 2.4.63 from signed RHEL repositories without changing the RHEL 10.0 release or kernel.
Created exact name-based virtual hosts with a deny-by-default virtual host.
Applied persistent SELinux content labels and an http_port_t assignment for TCP 8080.
Added TCP 8080 to firewalld and enabled Apache at boot.
Retained a root-only rollback copy at /root/httpd.conf.pre-name-based-tenants.
Removed test residue and completed post-reboot verification.

evidence.requirement: Serve the supplied docs and orders trees by hostname on shared TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Apache validates both named virtual hosts on 8080; all supplied resources return HTTP 200 and byte-identical SHA-256 hashes before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Unknown hosts must receive an error and tenants must remain isolated
evidence.summary: Unknown, IP-based, and look-alike Host values return HTTP 403; cross-tenant file requests return HTTP 404; final smoke tests repeat the expected behavior.
Pre-change and post-reboot checksums, ownership, modes, sizes, and paths match for every supplied file.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed OS release, kernel, security controls, and administrative access
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remain installed; SELinux is enforcing, firewalld persistently permits only the new 8080 port, and SSH remains active.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID a3e8d9cc-3426-483b-bee1-33f061401189 was captured; systemd acknowledged the safe delayed reboot; node1 returned with changed boot ID 8e2364fc-32de-44ee-bdc2-eb1c38edea4e; Apache, SSH, firewall, SELinux, content, and all routing behavior recovered.
